title: Samsung LPDDR5X-PIM at Hot Chips 2026
gist: Samsung unveiled LPDDR5X-PIM at Hot Chips 2026, the first LPDDR-based processing-in-memory product, pitching it as a lower-cost, lower-power alternative to HBM (which grew from 52% to 63% of AI chip component cost between Q1 2024 and Q4 2025) and backing the pitch with silicon-validated 2.28x latency and 3.01x tokens/sec gains on Llama-3.1-8B inference. STH's Patrick Kennedy sees adoption hinging on a large anchor customer and on JEDEC standardization to enable second-sourcing, since PIM hands memory vendors leverage over the compute side.

themes.theme: HBM Cost Pressure as the Opening for PIM

insights.claim: HBM's share of AI chip component spending rose from 52% in Q1 2024 to 63% by Q4 2025 and is likely higher now, making memory the dominant cost line in AI packages.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Rising HBM cost share is the economic wedge for HBM alternatives — watch memory vendors' non-HBM AI memory roadmaps and HBM pricing power.
insights.quote: HBM now claims the majority of AI chip component spending, and that share grew from 52 percent in Q1 2024 to 63 percent by Q4 2025.
insights.locator: Samsung opens with a market-context figure

insights.claim: Samsung is explicitly positioning LPDDR5X-PIM as a lower-cost, lower-power alternative to HBM for AI inference, arguing HBM's bandwidth comes with high power consumption and complex packaging.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: A credible LPDDR-based inference memory tier could cap HBM demand growth at the edge/inference end of the market — a risk factor for pure HBM bulls.
insights.quote: Samsung argues the route to lower cost runs through a new memory form factor the LP-PIM.
insights.locator: HBM delivers the bandwidth AI inference needs

insights.claim: Samsung's LPDDR5X-PIM is the world's first LPDDR-based processing-in-memory solution, productized in 2026 after a PIM lineage starting with the Aquabolt-XL HBM2-PIM proof of concept in 2021.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Five years from proof-of-concept to product signals PIM is exiting the research phase; first-mover status gives Samsung a lead over SK hynix/Micron in this niche.
insights.locator: Here Samsung traces its PIM timeline

insights.claim: LPDDR5X-PIM delivers 614 GB/s of internal PIM bandwidth at the x64 9600 Mbps operating point — eight times the 76.8 GB/s available on the conventional DRAM interface — in a JEDEC-standard 561-ball, 16 GB package targeting server, mobile, and client.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: An 8x effective bandwidth uplift inside a standard LPDDR package is the core technical claim to evaluate against HBM economics for bandwidth-bound inference.
insights.quote: PIM bandwidth reaches 614 GB/s at the x64 9600 Mbps operating point, eight times the 76.8 GB/s available on the conventional DRAM side.
insights.locator: This specification figure shows a JEDEC-standard

insights.claim: LPDDR5X-PIM is the first LP-PIM product with multi-precision support — fifteen selectable datatype combinations — reaching 2.4 TOPS with SINT4 weights or roughly 1.2 TFLOPs per package in FP8.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Multi-precision support aligns PIM with the low-bit quantization trend in inference; per-package compute figures let analysts model system-level TOPS from memory alone.
insights.locator: LPDDR5X-PIM is the first LP-PIM product

insights.claim: Address Align Mode maps DRAM addresses to MAC instructions so LPDDR5X-PIM works with a conventional DRAM controller, removing the need for custom controller silicon and lowering the adoption barrier for SoC designers.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Drop-in compatibility is the classic adoption unlock for new memory tech — it means existing SoCs can trial PIM without a redesign cycle, accelerating potential uptake.
insights.quote: This mapping between DRAM addresses and MAC instructions lets LPDDR5X-PIM work with a conventional DRAM controller rather than requiring a new one.
insights.locator: Drop-in compatibility rests on Address Align Mode

insights.claim: Samsung says its new mode-change mechanism (predefined rows and PIM registers switching between single-bank and multi-bank PIM operation) is faster and more reliable than the HBM-PIM approach of prior generations.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Iterative fixes to prior PIM generations' pain points suggest Samsung is engineering for productization, not another demo — a maturity signal.
insights.locator: Mode change shuttles the part between

insights.claim: On Samsung's edge AI accelerator SoC running Llama-3.1-8B (320-token context, SINT8 activations, SINT4 weights), LPDDR5X-PIM finished in 5.4 seconds versus 12.3 seconds on conventional LPDDR5X — a 2.28x gain — with throughput up 3.01x to 81.3 tokens/sec from 27.0.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: These are measured-on-silicon, not simulated, numbers — a 2-3x edge-inference uplift from memory alone reshapes edge AI accelerator design math and on-device LLM feasibility.
insights.quote: This LPDDR5X-PIM build finished the run in 5.4 seconds against 12.3 seconds on conventional LPDDR5X, a 2.28x gain, and output climbed to 81.3 tokens per second from 27.0, a 3.01x gain.
insights.locator: Samsung validated the design on silicon

themes.theme: Path to Adoption: Ecosystem and Standardization

insights.claim: Samsung is shipping software alongside the hardware — a simulator and datasheet on request plus an SDK with reference tooling — while LPDDR6-PIM moves toward a finalized JEDEC LP6-PIM specification.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: A JEDEC LP6-PIM standard would move PIM from proprietary Samsung tech to an industry category — watch the spec's finalization as the key adoption milestone.
insights.quote: LPDDR6-PIM moves toward a finalized JEDEC LP6-PIM specification.
insights.locator: Samsung made clear that software is part

insights.claim: PIM adoption likely requires a large anchor customer to demand and implement it before it spreads widely; the measured gains make Samsung's pitch concrete but do not by themselves drive adoption.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Watch for a named lead customer (a hyperscaler or major edge-device OEM) as the catalyst that turns PIM from conference demo into revenue.
insights.quote: This one feels like one where a large customer is going to have to come in and say this is needed, implement it, and then it will get widely adopted.

insights.claim: Putting compute inside memory gives memory vendors leverage over customers by controlling both the memory and compute sides, so buyers will demand standardization to enable second-sourcing before committing to PIM.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: This supplier-leverage dynamic explains why JEDEC standardization is the gating factor, and why PIM could raise memory vendors' margins/moats if it succeeds.
insights.quote: if you give a memory vendor not just control over the memory but also the compute side, they have more leverage with their customers. You need standardization at least so a vendor can second source.
